study.question: With the context/history interaction route held sign-canonical, is the earlier residual-adapter recovery from signed coarse history moments primarily direct click-head use, auxiliary-to-context transfer, or interaction between task groups?
study.hypothesis: g1-r0070-adapter_signed recovers95.6936% of the contemporaneous both-axis/both-signed gap, contradicting the previous dominant-product-route expectation. Hypothesis: direct click-adapter sign access accounts for>=75% of the adapter-specific endpoint gap, with auxiliary-adapter access alone accounting for<=25%. Auxiliary heads can still affect click learning through allowed shared-context gradients, so this must be tested rather than assumed. This attributes one learned coarse-moment representation under one frozen seed/recipe; other order-sensitive channels remain.
